corrections.why: The FFLA Idaho list marks the lookout Standing, and firelookout.com says the cab is still there. The brief's gone came from the abandonment, which is not the same as removal.
The register and the FFLA Idaho list both give 44.89312, -114.80511. The brief's point is about 74 km away.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three sources give a 10 by 10 foot cab or groundhouse. Forest Lookouts gives a two-story 12 by 12 log cabin. All four history sources agree the cab was built in 1934. The story reports both sizes.

The register gives Salmon-Challis National Forest, while firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts give Salmon National Forest. A 1945 survey description on Forest Lookouts places a Bear Creek Pt. lookout tower in the Nez Perce National Forest. It may be a different point with the same name.
Abandoned in the 1950s, but still standing by the FFLA list and firelookout.com, which is undated. Both can be true, so the record uses standing and dates the abandonment to the 1950s.

notes_for_editor: Duplicate record: us-id-bear-creek-point-2 covers the same lookout with the NHLR coordinates and already has research and a story. Merge the two before publishing. us-id-bear-creek is a different lookout in Bonner County. Status: FFLA says Standing and firelookout.com says still there, but firelookout.com is undated and no 2020s source checked the cab. Access level is left unset: the sources give trail-only and wilderness status, not open or closed. The brief's height_m of 3.0 has no support and is omitted. No notable fires were found. The 1951 item does not clearly name this site, and the 1945 survey may describe a different point. Elevation 8,629 ft (2,630 m) is in NHLR but has no key in this schema.
